solution: Use inclusion–exclusion to enforce no fixed points. For a specified set S of k positions required to be fixed, delete those positions and values. The remaining permutation has n=9−k elements, and its left-to-right maxima are unchanged: each deleted fixed value i occurs at position i, so it cannot be a left-to-right maximum unless all earlier values are smaller, while in that case the same record is already represented by the induced order on the remaining values. Equivalently, for this fixed-point inclusion–exclusion, count permutations of the remaining ordered values with the same record count, giving c(n,3), the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind. insight: The number of permutations of n elements with exactly r left-to-right maxima is the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind c(n,r).
insight_justification: Inserting the largest element into a permutation of n−1 elements creates a new record when placed first; the other n−1 insertion slots preserve the record count. Hence c(n,r)=c(n−1,r−1)+(n−1)c(n−1,r).
